name: Rotech
desc:
Medical Billing & Collections Generalist | $15 to $17/hr | Claims Follow-Up and Data Entry, Some Phone Calls, No Sales Expectations
Company: Rotech Healthcare Inc.
Industry: Health Science

What Your Day Will Look Like:
Rotech provides home medical equipment like oxygen, CPAP machines, and ventilators. In this role, you work in Rotech's Billing Center figuring out why insurance claims haven't been paid and getting them fixed. You'll review patient information in Rotech's billing systems, process doctor and insurance changes, make adjustments, and re-bill claims after your supervisor approves them. When needed, you'll contact the insurance company, the patient, or a Rotech location to sort things out, and you'll note every step. You'll report payer trends that are holding up payments and take on special projects from your supervisor. It's a steady Monday through Friday schedule with flexible hours.

Soft Skills
- Attention to detail
- Problem solving
- Organization and time management
- Clear, professional communication
- Working independently
assessment: Expect an assessment involving a typing test
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements

Education Minimum: High school diploma or GED
Required Experience: None required
Preferred Experience: 1 to 3 years of related work on a team, medical field and records experience, and a strong customer service background

Required Skills:
- Clear written and verbal English
- Keeping sensitive information confidential
- Multitasking with attention to detail
- Self-motivated and organized
- Problem solving
- Microsoft Outlook, Word, and Excel
- Comfortable researching online

This role is ideal for someone who:
- Has medical billing training or medical office experience
- Likes figuring out why something went wrong and fixing it
- Wants a Monday through Friday daytime schedule
- Is organized and keeps careful notes

Not a Good Fit for someone who:
- Doesn't want to talk with patients about unpaid bills
- Gets bored with detailed computer work
- Needs evening or weekend hours
- Struggles to meet deadlines
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
1. Submit application
2. Expect an assessment email
3. Watch for an email inviting you to a prescreening
4. Depending on how well the prescreening went, expect an email to schedule an interview
This is an estimated process. Rotech says hiring managers review resumes and reach out to applicants who match.

Top 10 Resume Keywords
- Medical billing
- Insurance claims follow-up
- Collections
- Claim adjustments
- Re-billing
- Payer communication
- Data entry
- HIPAA and confidentiality
- Microsoft Excel
- Problem solving

4-5 Interview Questions for this Role:
- Tell us about any medical billing or medical office experience you have.
- A claim came back unpaid. How would you figure out why?
- How do you keep track of many accounts and deadlines at once?
- Tell us about a time you found and fixed a mistake. What happened, what did you do, and what was the result?
- Tell us about a time you had to call someone to resolve a problem. What was the situation, what did you do, and how did it turn out?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
-Pay: $15 to $17/hr, based on experience and the state you're hired in.
-Shift: Monday through Friday, with flexible hours between 7:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. The posting doesn't say which time zone, so confirm in the interview.
-Benefits: Generous PTO and paid holidays, 401(k), HSA, FSA, medical, prescription, dental, and vision, life and disability insurance, EAP, and mental health and chronic condition programs.
-Equipment Provided: Not stated in the posting. Ask in the interview.
-Felony Friendly?: Case by case. Rotech does a background check but says results won't automatically disqualify anyone. They look at the role, the offense, how long ago it was, and evidence of rehabilitation.
-Drug Test: Certain positions
-Notes: This position is available in Oklahoma. It's a good fit for participants with medical billing training who want a weekday schedule. The work is mostly insurance claim follow-up, with some contact with patients about unpaid balances. The background policy is friendly to second-chance candidates. Training length and camera requirements are not listed.
-Career Pathway: Reasonable inferred path: Billing & Collections Generalist → Senior Billing Specialist → Billing Team Lead → Billing Center Supervisor. This role builds medical billing, claims, and healthcare revenue cycle skills.
